cell_types.name: Definitive endoderm
cell_types.summary: Definitive endoderm is the germ layer that gives rise to liver, pancreas, gut, lung, thyroid and thymus. hPSC-derived endoderm is the mandatory first step of every protocol in this group and is also used on its own to test a line's endoderm competence.
cell_types.maturation_note: Usable at day 3 (short small-molecule/Activin protocols) to day 5 (Activin-only protocols); it is a transient population and should be patterned onwards immediately.

morphology.endpoint: A flat, confluent sheet of fairly uniform cells that are larger and less tightly packed than the starting hPSC, with no sharp colony borders left.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact colonies with sharp edges and small cells with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio.

stages.label: Streak-like cells leaving the colonies
stages.look: Colony borders dissolve as cells undergo an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition and spread outward; some floating dead cells are normal.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm sheet
stages.look: Original colonies are no longer recognisable; a continuous sheet of larger, slightly cobbled cells covers the well.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost within the first days of endoderm induction.

markers.name: NANOG
markers.note: Residual NANOG+ patches mean induction was incomplete, often because the starting culture was too dense.

markers.name: TBXT
markers.note: Transient at about 24 h; should be down again by the endoderm stage.

markers.name: MIXL1
markers.note: Transient streak marker; Loh 2014 report >99% MIXL1-GFP+ cells after 24 h.

markers.name: EOMES
markers.note: Early streak/endoderm transcription factor.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Core definitive endoderm transcription factor; check together with FOXA2.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX17 in definitive endoderm and retained in most endoderm derivatives.

markers.name: CXCR4
markers.note: Live-cell surface readout of endoderm induction; usually combined with KIT (CD117) or EPCAM.

markers.name: KIT
markers.note: CXCR4+/KIT+ double positivity is the usual flow gate for endoderm.

markers.name: GATA4
markers.note: Expressed in endoderm in the Si-Tayeb and Vallier protocols.

markers.name: PDGFRA
markers.note: Mesoderm marker; Loh 2014 score endoderm as CXCR4+ PDGFRA-.

markers.name: HNF4A
markers.note: Absent from day-5 definitive endoderm; presence at this stage suggests visceral endoderm (Si-Tayeb 2010).

functional_assays: Competence test: ability to give HNF4A+ hepatic, PDX1+ pancreatic or CDX2+ hindgut cells on further patterning
qc: CXCR4+ (with KIT or SOX17) >= 60% by flow before continuing; the Vallier protocols expect 60-90% and others >= 80-90%
SOX17+/FOXA2+ double-positive nuclei >= 85% by immunostaining (McCracken 2011)
FOXA2+/SOX17+ > 90% at the end of stage 1 for beta-cell differentiations (Hogrebe 2021)

protocols.name: Three-day serum-free induction: streak (Activin/CHIR/PI-103) then BMP block
protocols.principle: Anterior primitive streak is induced for 24 h with high Activin plus Wnt activation and PI3K inhibition, then BMP is inhibited while Activin continues so that streak cells become endoderm rather than mesoderm.

source.authors: Loh KM, Ang LT, Zhang J, et al.
source.title: Efficient endoderm induction from human pluripotent stem cells by logically directing signals controlling lineage bifurcations

protocols.efficiency: 94.0 ± 3.1% CXCR4+PDGFRA- definitive endoderm by day 3 across 9 hESC and hiPSC lines
protocols.start_requirements: mTeSR1-grown hPSC passaged about 1:3 as small clumps (collagenase IV) onto fibronectin- or Matrigel-coated plates; start 1-2 days later.

stages.name: Anterior primitive streak
stages.base_medium: CDM2 (serum-free chemically defined basal medium of the paper)

factors.name: Activin A
factors.role: Nodal/TGF-beta signal; drives primitive streak and endoderm

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; Wnt activation for streak induction (first 24 h only)

actions: Wash the cells before adding induction medium
Treat for exactly 24 h
stages.checkpoint: MIXL1/BRACHYURY+ streak-like cells; colonies loosen and cells spread

stages.name: Definitive endoderm
stages.base_medium: CDM2

factors.name: DM3189 (LDN-193189)
factors.role: BMP inhibitor; blocks the mesoderm alternative

actions: Remove CHIR and PI-103
Keep BMP inhibited for the full 48 h
stages.checkpoint: CXCR4+ PDGFRA- cells with SOX17 and FOXA2 in most nuclei (94 ± 3% CXCR4+PDGFRA- reported across nine lines)

materials: CDM2 basal medium (recipe in the paper's supplement)
tips: Timing is strict: the Wnt/PI3K-inhibitor pulse is 24 h, then BMP inhibition for 48 h.
The same paper continues to foregut (A-83-01 + DM3189), posterior foregut (RA + DM3189) or mid/hindgut (BMP4 10 ng/mL, CHIR 3 µM, FGF2 100 ng/mL) for 4 more days.
pitfalls: BMP present during days 1-3 diverts streak cells to mesoderm.
CDM2 composition must be taken from the supplement; substituting another basal medium changes efficiency.
unverified: Exact CDM2 recipe and seeding density are in the supplemental procedures, which were not read.

protocols.name: Chemically defined Activin/FGF2/BMP4/LY294002/CHIR induction (Vallier lab)
protocols.principle: Activin with FGF2, BMP4 and PI3K inhibition drives hPSC through a streak-like state; a one-day CHIR pulse boosts mesendoderm, and a final day in RPMI/B-27 with Activin and FGF2 commits the cells to endoderm.

source.authors: Hannan NR, Segeritz CP, Touboul T, Vallier L
source.title: Production of hepatocyte-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow after 3 days
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in chemically defined medium with Activin A (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL); passaged as small clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin plates pre-coated with serum-containing medium and grown for about 2 days before induction (the paper calls plating 'day 0' and the first induction day 'day 2').

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 1
stages.base_medium: CDM-PVA
actions: Add all factors fresh to the medium on the day
Never carry CHIR99021 beyond the first day
stages.checkpoint: Cells migrate out of the colonies (EMT); T, MIXL1 and EOMES are induced

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 2
stages.base_medium: CDM-PVA
actions: Replace with the same medium without CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: Original colony outlines are gone; SOX17 and CXCR4 switch on as T and MIXL1 fall

stages.name: Endoderm commitment, day 3
actions: Switch basal medium to RPMI/B-27
stages.checkpoint: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow at the end of this day

tips: Add growth factors fresh each day rather than making bulk medium.
Optimise the FGF2 and CHIR99021 doses for each new line; the authors name this as the main lever for poor lines.
The later protocol from the same lab (Sampaziotis 2017) uses the same recipe with FGF2 at 80 ng/mL and reports >90% SOX17+.
pitfalls: About 20% of hiPSC lines were resistant to endoderm induction in the authors' hands.
Cell death on days 1-2 is expected; if it is excessive, lower the LY294002 dose.

protocols.name: Activin A with stepped serum (D'Amour-style, as written out by the Wells lab)
protocols.principle: High Activin A in RPMI with serum raised stepwise from 0 to 2% mimics Nodal signalling while keeping PI3K/insulin signalling low; this is the low-serum Activin approach introduced by D'Amour et al. 2005 (Nat Biotechnol, PMID 16258519), in the form used for gut organoid work.

source.authors: McCracken KW, Howell JC, Wells JM, Spence JR
source.title: Generating human intestinal tissue from pluripotent stem cells in vitro

protocols.efficiency: 85-90% SOX17+/FOXA2+ double-positive cells
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC on hESC-qualified Matrigel in mTeSR1, passaged with dispase into 24-well plates and grown to about 85-90% confluence with minimal spontaneous differentiation.

stages.name: Day 1: Activin, no serum
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 2 mM L-glutamine + pen/strep
actions: Aspirate mTeSR1 and add day-1 medium
Use no serum on the first day
stages.checkpoint: Cells begin to spread; some death is normal

stages.name: Day 2: Activin + 0.2% serum
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 2 mM L-glutamine + 0.2% defined FBS
actions: Change to day-2 medium

stages.name: Day 3: Activin + 2% serum
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 + 2 mM L-glutamine + 2% defined FBS
actions: Change to day-3 medium
Optionally stain a coverslip for SOX17/FOXA2 at the end
stages.checkpoint: 85-90% SOX17+/FOXA2+ nuclei

tips: Make the Activin media fresh each day if possible.
The updated Wells-lab protocol (Broda 2019) plates single cells with Y-27632 the day before, adds NEAA, and includes BMP4 50 ng/mL on the first day only.
pitfalls: Starting density is the main failure point: too dense leaves undifferentiated patches, too sparse never reaches a usable sheet.
Serum lot matters; the authors specify defined FBS.
unverified: The original D'Amour 2005 methods text could not be opened (paywalled); only its abstract (Activin A plus low serum, up to 80% endoderm, CXCR4 enrichment) was confirmed. The day-by-day recipe here is from McCracken 2011.

cell_types.notes: All three routes work; pick the one that matches the downstream protocol you intend to follow, because later stages were tuned to their own endoderm. Endoderm efficiency varies between lines more than any later step, so titrate starting density (and CHIR/FGF2 where used) on every new line and check CXCR4 or SOX17/FOXA2 before committing weeks of culture. A CHIR99021-only, growth-factor-free endoderm step (Siller 2015) and a 4-day Activin/CHIR step in MCDB131 (Hogrebe 2021) are described under hepatocytes and beta cells.

cell_types.name: Hepatocyte-like cells
cell_types.summary: Hepatocytes are the parenchymal cells of the liver responsible for plasma protein secretion, drug metabolism, and lipid and glycogen handling. hPSC-derived hepatocyte-like cells are used for metabolic disease modelling, hepatotoxicity testing and as a prospective cell-therapy source, although they remain fetal-like.
cell_types.maturation_note: Polygonal morphology from about day 15; albumin and A1AT secretion from about day 15 and inducible P450 activity from about day 20 (Hannan 2013). Cells keep AFP and CYP3A7 and survive only a few weeks.

morphology.endpoint: A tight sheet of polygonal cells with dark granular cytoplasm, round pale nuclei (some cells binucleate) and bright refractile borders resembling bile canaliculi; lipid droplets appear with time.

stages.label: Pluripotent colonies
stages.look: Compact, sharp-edged colonies of small cells.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm
stages.look: Colonies have dispersed into a continuous sheet of larger, flatter cells.

stages.label: Hepatic endoderm
stages.look: A cobblestone epithelium of polygonal cells forms as the sheet re-epithelialises.

stages.label: Hepatoblasts
stages.look: Cells darken, nuclei look pale and round, and bright cell borders begin to appear.

stages.label: Hepatocyte-like cells
stages.look: Polygonal, sometimes binucleate cells with canaliculi-like bright borders and lipid vesicles.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost within the first days of endoderm induction.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Core definitive endoderm transcription factor; check together with FOXA2.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX17 in definitive endoderm and retained in most endoderm derivatives.

markers.name: HNF4A
markers.note: Switches on at hepatic specification; >80-90% of cells expected.

markers.name: AFP
markers.note: Fetal marker; stays high in hPSC-derived cells and falls only partially with maturation.

markers.name: TBX3
markers.note: Hepatoblast transcription factor used to monitor specification.

markers.name: ALB
markers.note: Main readout; about 80% ALB+ by flow in Si-Tayeb 2010; secreted albumin measurable by ELISA.

markers.name: SERPINA1
markers.note: Co-stained with albumin; also the disease readout in A1AT-deficiency models.

markers.name: KRT18
markers.note: Hepatocyte cytokeratin, co-stained with albumin.

markers.name: TTR
markers.note: Hepatic secreted protein.

markers.name: CYP3A4
markers.note: Adult P450; activity is well below primary hepatocytes.

markers.name: CYP3A7
markers.note: Fetal P450; persistent expression shows the fetal-like state of the cells.

qc: Endoderm: >= 60% CXCR4+/SOX17+ before hepatic specification (Hannan 2013)
HNF4A+ in about 90% of cells at the hepatic endoderm stage (Hannan 2013)
Albumin+ about 80% by flow at the end of the Si-Tayeb protocol
AFP+/HNF4A+ 86-89% at the end of the DMSO stage (Siller 2015)

protocols.name: Four 5-day stages: Activin, BMP4/FGF2, HGF, oncostatin M (Duncan lab)
protocols.principle: Mimics liver development in four growth-factor steps of five days each, with the middle stages run at 4% oxygen: Activin for endoderm, BMP4 plus FGF2 for hepatic specification, HGF for hepatoblast expansion and oncostatin M for maturation.

source.authors: Si-Tayeb K, Noto FK, Nagaoka M, et al.
source.title: Highly efficient generation of human hepatocyte-like cells from induced pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: About 80-85% albumin-positive cells by flow cytometry (hESC and hiPSC)
protocols.start_requirements: Feeder-free monolayer on Matrigel in MEF-conditioned hESC medium, maintained at 4% O2 / 5% CO2; >95% OCT4+ at the start.

stages.name: Definitive endoderm
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Move the cultures to ambient oxygen / 5% CO2 for this stage
stages.checkpoint: >80% FOXA2+, GATA4+, SOX17+; OCT4 lost in >90% of cells; HNF4A still negative

stages.name: Hepatic specification
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Move the cultures to 4% O2 / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: >80% HNF4A+; GATA4 and SOX17 fall while FOXA2 persists

stages.name: Hepatoblast expansion
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Keep at 4% O2 / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: Strong AFP in nearly all FOXA2+ cells

stages.name: Hepatocyte maturation
stages.base_medium: Hepatocyte Culture Medium (HCM)
stages.feeding: Not stated in the main text
actions: Return the cultures to ambient oxygen / 5% CO2
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal, partly binucleate albumin+ cells; albumin detectable in medium

tips: Needs a tri-gas incubator for the 4% oxygen steps.
Works as a true monolayer without embryoid bodies or serum.
pitfalls: Cells remain fetal-like (AFP stays high).
Small timing differences in marker onset between hESC and hiPSC lines were noted by the authors.
unverified: Feeding frequency, B-27 type and seeding density are in the supplementary methods, which were not read.

protocols.name: Chemically defined route via anterior endoderm (Vallier lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm made with Activin/FGF2/BMP4/LY294002/CHIR is anteriorised with Activin alone, specified to hepatic endoderm with BMP4 and FGF10, and matured with oncostatin M and HGF.

source.authors: Hannan NR, Segeritz CP, Touboul T, Vallier L
source.title: Production of hepatocyte-like cells from human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: Under optimal conditions >85% ALB+/A1AT+ cells; about 15 million immature hepatocytes from 600,000 hPSC plated on a 10 cm dish
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in chemically defined medium with Activin A (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL); passaged as small clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin plates pre-coated with serum-containing medium and grown for about 2 days before induction (the paper calls plating 'day 0' and the first induction day 'day 2').

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 1
stages.base_medium: CDM-PVA
actions: Add all factors fresh to the medium on the day
Never carry CHIR99021 beyond the first day
stages.checkpoint: Cells migrate out of the colonies (EMT); T, MIXL1 and EOMES are induced

stages.name: Endoderm induction, day 2
stages.base_medium: CDM-PVA
actions: Replace with the same medium without CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: Original colony outlines are gone; SOX17 and CXCR4 switch on as T and MIXL1 fall

stages.name: Endoderm commitment, day 3
actions: Switch basal medium to RPMI/B-27
stages.checkpoint: 60-90% CXCR4+ and/or SOX17+ by flow at the end of this day

stages.name: Anterior definitive endoderm
actions: Feed every 24 h
stages.checkpoint: Cells re-epithelialise into a monolayer expressing FOXA2 and HHEX

stages.name: Hepatic specification
stages.feeding: Daily for 3 days, then leave a further 24 h
actions: Monitor HNF4A, PROX1, HHEX, AFP and TBX3 by qPCR
stages.checkpoint: About 90% HNF4A+ cells; dark cytoplasm and pale nuclei

stages.name: Hepatocyte maturation
stages.base_medium: Hepatocyte Basal Medium (Lonza CC-3199) prepared with its supplement kit
actions: Assay protein secretion, P450 activity, LDL uptake and glycogen between about days 18 and 28 of differentiation
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal, multinucleated cells with canaliculi-like borders from about day 13; albumin and A1AT in the medium

tips: The paper counts days from plating, so its 'day 25' endpoint is day 23 here.
If BMP4 harms hepatoblast specification in a given line, the authors replace that stage with 3 extra days of Activin in RPMI/B-27.
pitfalls: About 20% of hiPSC lines failed at the endoderm step.
Survival beyond the assay window varies by line; the troubleshooting table notes HepatoZYME can replace the Lonza basal medium if a line responds poorly.

protocols.name: Growth-factor-free: CHIR99021, DMSO, then dexamethasone + dihexa
protocols.principle: A 24 h GSK3-inhibitor pulse is enough to make endoderm, DMSO specifies hepatic progenitors, and dexamethasone with the HGF-receptor agonist dihexa replaces HGF/oncostatin M for maturation.

source.authors: Siller R, Greenhough S, Naumovska E, Sullivan GJ
source.title: Small-molecule-driven hepatocyte differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells

protocols.efficiency: 86-89% AFP+/HNF4A+ hepatic progenitors after the DMSO stage
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC in Essential 8 on growth-factor-reduced Matrigel, passaged with 0.5 mM EDTA; seeded at a 1:3-1:4 split into Matrigel-coated 12-well plates and started 24 h later. Optimal density must be set per line.

stages.name: Phase I: CHIR pulse
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 GlutaMAX + B-27 (with or without insulin)

factors.name: CHIR99021
factors.role: GSK3 inhibitor; drives cells through primitive streak to endoderm

actions: Wash with PBS, then add CHIR medium
Use 3 µM for H1; 4 µM in B-27 minus insulin was best for the other lines tested

stages.name: Phase I: rest
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640 GlutaMAX + B-27
actions: Remove CHIR99021
stages.checkpoint: FOXA2+/SOX17+ endoderm with raised HHEX, CER1 and GSC

stages.name: Phase II: hepatic specification
stages.base_medium: KnockOut DMEM + 20% KnockOut Serum Replacement + 2 mM GlutaMAX + 100 µM 2-mercaptoethanol + 1x NEAA
actions: Expect a burst of proliferation and a rapid change in morphology
stages.checkpoint: 86-89% AFP+/HNF4A+ cells

stages.name: Phase III: maturation
stages.base_medium: Leibovitz L-15 + 8.3% tryptose phosphate broth + 8.3% FBS + 10 µM hydrocortisone 21-hemisuccinate + 50 µg/mL sodium L-ascorbate + 0.58% ITS + 2 mM GlutaMAX
actions: Culture for 10 days
stages.checkpoint: Polygonal albumin+/HNF4A+ cells with A1AT, glycogen storage and ICG uptake

tips: Cheap: no recombinant growth factors.
Titrate CHIR99021 (the authors tested 1-10 µM) and the insulin content of B-27 on each new line.
pitfalls: Dihexa was a gift from its inventor in the paper and is not a standard catalogue reagent everywhere; check supply before starting.
The maturation medium contains FBS, so the method is growth-factor-free but not serum-free.
unverified: Final percentage of albumin-positive cells is given in a figure and was not captured.

cell_types.notes: All published hepatocyte-like cells are immature compared with primary adult hepatocytes: AFP and CYP3A7 persist and P450 activity is low. Efficiency is governed by the endoderm step and by cell density; test each line. The Mallanna & Duncan 2013 Current Protocols version of the Si-Tayeb method could not be located in PubMed during this search and is not cited.

cell_types.name: Liver organoids / liver buds
cell_types.summary: Liver organoids are three-dimensional hepatic tissues grown from hPSC-derived foregut cells; depending on the method they contain hepatocyte-like cells alone or together with stellate-like, Kupffer-like and biliary cells, or are built by mixing hepatic endoderm with endothelial and mesenchymal cells (liver buds). They are used to model steatohepatitis and fibrosis, to screen for drug-induced liver injury, and as transplantable tissue.
cell_types.maturation_note: Organoids are analysed between about day 20 and day 30; bile-acid transport and CYP3A4 induction are measurable at that point.

morphology.endpoint: Translucent epithelial cysts and denser spheres, roughly 100-300 µm across, embedded in a Matrigel drop; lumens are visible in many organoids.

stages.label: Pluripotent cells
stages.look: Single-cell-seeded hPSC that grow into a dense layer of small cells.

stages.label: Definitive endoderm
stages.look: Continuous sheet of flatter, larger cells.

stages.label: Foregut spheroids
stages.look: Three-dimensional buds rise from the sheet and detach as small spheroids.

stages.label: Embedded organoids
stages.look: Spheroids in Matrigel enlarge and hollow out during retinoic acid treatment.

stages.label: Liver organoids
stages.look: Cystic and dense epithelial organoids with visible lumens fill the Matrigel drop.

markers.name: POU5F1
markers.note: Should be lost within the first days of endoderm induction.

markers.name: SOX17
markers.note: Core definitive endoderm transcription factor; check together with FOXA2.

markers.name: FOXA2
markers.note: Co-expressed with SOX17 in definitive endoderm and retained in most endoderm derivatives.

markers.name: EPCAM
markers.note: Epithelial fraction: about 79% of organoid cells in Ouchi 2019.

markers.name: ALB
markers.note: Secreted albumin is the routine functional readout.

markers.name: HNF4A
markers.note: Hepatocyte identity.

markers.name: CYP3A4
markers.note: Induced by rifampicin in Ouchi 2019.

markers.name: CYP7A1
markers.note: Bile-acid synthesis enzyme reported in Shinozawa 2021 organoids.

markers.name: ALCAM
markers.note: Stellate-like cells: EpCAM-negative CD166+ stellate-like fraction (about 7% of cells in Ouchi 2019).

markers.name: VIM
markers.note: Stellate-like cells: Mesenchymal/stellate-like cells.

markers.name: DES
markers.note: Stellate-like cells: Stellate marker.

markers.name: CD68
markers.note: Kupffer-like cells: Macrophage-like cells present in multicellular organoids.

functional_assays: Bile-acid uptake and efflux with fluorescent bile acids (CLF, CGamF)
Organoid stiffness by atomic force microscopy (fibrosis model)
Vitamin A autofluorescence of stellate-like cells
qc: EpCAM+ fraction about 79 ± 7% of organoid cells (Ouchi 2019)
Spheroids must be visible by day 6 before embedding

protocols.name: Multicellular human liver organoids from foregut spheroids (Takebe lab)
protocols.principle: Endoderm is posteriorised with FGF4 and CHIR until it buds into foregut spheroids; these are embedded in Matrigel, pulsed with retinoic acid, and matured in hepatocyte medium, which yields hepatocyte-like cells together with stellate-like and Kupffer-like cells.

source.authors: Ouchi R, Togo S, Kimura M, et al.
source.title: Modeling Steatohepatitis in Humans with Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Organoids

protocols.efficiency: EpCAM+ epithelial cells 78.9 ± 7.4% of organoid cells; EpCAM-CD166+ stellate-like cells about 7%
protocols.start_requirements: hPSC dissociated with Accutase; 200,000 cells seeded on Matrigel- or iMatrix-coated plates (day 0). The paper numbers the first Activin day as day 1.

stages.name: Definitive endoderm
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640
actions: Seed 200,000 Accutase-dissociated cells the day before
Day 1: Activin A + BMP4, no serum
Day 2: Activin A + 0.2% FCS
Day 3: Activin A + 2% FCS

stages.name: Posterior foregut spheroids
stages.base_medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 + B-27 + N-2
actions: Feed daily through day 6
stages.checkpoint: Budding spheroids appear on the monolayer by day 6

stages.name: Embedding and retinoic acid
stages.base_medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 + B-27 + N-2

factors.name: Retinoic acid
factors.role: Patterns foregut towards a hepatic fate

actions: Pipette gently to lift spheroids and attached cells
Spin at 800 rpm for 3 min
Embed in a 100% Matrigel drop
Culture 4 days

stages.name: Hepatic maturation
stages.base_medium: Hepatocyte Culture Medium (HCM, Lonza)
actions: Culture to day 20-30
Release organoids by scratching and pipetting the Matrigel for assays
stages.checkpoint: Cystic organoids; albumin secretion and CYP3A4 inducibility

tips: For steatohepatitis modelling the organoids are freed from Matrigel and exposed to oleic acid (up to 800 µM) on ultra-low-attachment plates for 3-7 days.
Spheroid yield at day 6 is the practical go/no-go point.
pitfalls: The wording 'day 4-6' for the FGF4/CHIR step can be read as 2 or 3 days; spheroids are collected on day 6.
Organoid composition (parenchymal versus stellate-like and Kupffer-like cells) varies between lines.
unverified: Plate format for the 200,000-cell seeding and feeding interval during the retinoic acid step are not stated in the main methods.

protocols.name: Bankable foregut cells to liver organoids for toxicity screening (Takebe lab)
protocols.principle: The same endoderm and FGF4/CHIR foregut steps are run on laminin, the foregut cells are frozen as a bank, and thawed cells are embedded in Matrigel and taken through organoid formation, liver specification and maturation media to give organoids with bile-acid transport suited to 384-well imaging.

source.authors: Shinozawa T, Kimura M, Cai Y, et al.
source.title: High-Fidelity Drug-Induced Liver Injury Screen Using Human Pluripotent Stem Cell-Derived Organoids

protocols.start_requirements: hiPSC dissociated with Accutase and seeded at 100,000 cells/cm2 on laminin-coated plates (day 0).

stages.name: Definitive endoderm
stages.base_medium: RPMI 1640
actions: Day 1: Activin A + BMP4
Day 2: Activin A + 0.2% FCS
Day 3: Activin A + 2% FCS

stages.name: Foregut
stages.base_medium: Advanced DMEM/F12 + B-27 + N-2
actions: Detach foregut cells with Accutase
Freeze in Cell Banker 1 if a bank is wanted

stages.name: Organoid formation
stages.base_medium: Organoid formation medium (composition in the paper's supplementary methods)

factors.name: 'Five-factor' organoid formation supplement
factors.role: Not specified in the main text

actions: Thaw foregut cells
Embed 100,000 cells per 50 µL Matrigel drop
Culture 4 days

stages.name: Liver specification
stages.base_medium: Liver specification medium (composition in the supplementary methods)

factors.name: Liver specification factors
factors.role: Not specified in the main text

actions: Culture 4 days
Then release organoids from Matrigel by scratching and pipetting

stages.name: Liver maturation
stages.base_medium: Liver maturation medium (composition in the supplementary methods)

factors.name: Liver maturation factors
factors.role: Not specified in the main text

actions: Re-embed in Matrigel on ultra-low-attachment plates
Culture 10 days
stages.checkpoint: Organoids take up and excrete fluorescent bile acids into the lumen

tips: Freezing at the foregut stage lets many organoid batches start from one validated endoderm run.
In the screening format organoids were moved to floating culture at day 15 and dispensed at about 15 per well of a 384-well plate at day 21.
pitfalls: Do not start this protocol without the supplementary methods: the three organoid media are defined only there.
unverified: Compositions of the organoid formation ('5 factors'), liver specification and liver maturation media are in the supplementary methods and were not confirmed.
No overall efficiency figure was captured.

cell_types.notes: The landmark liver-bud method (Takebe 2013 Nature, PMID 23823721; protocol in Takebe 2014 Nat Protoc, PMID 24457331, doi 10.1038/nprot.2014.020) mixes iPSC-derived hepatic endoderm with endothelial cells and mesenchymal stem cells on a pre-solidified matrix, where they condense into a 3D bud within 1-2 days that is transplanted at 4 days. Its cell numbers and media could not be opened here (paywalled), so it is not given as a step-by-step entry. An all-iPSC, animal-origin-free version exists (Sekine 2020 Sci Rep, PMID 33087763) but relies on proprietary supplements.

cell_types.name: Cholangiocytes (bile duct)
cell_types.summary: Cholangiocytes line the bile ducts, modify bile through secretion and absorption, and carry a primary cilium. hPSC-derived cholangiocytes are used to model cystic fibrosis liver disease, polycystic liver disease and other cholangiopathies, and to test CFTR modulators.
cell_types.maturation_note: Organoids form 2-4 days after transfer to 3D and are used at about day 26 (Sampaziotis 2017); ciliated, CFTR-functional monolayers take until about day 49 (Ogawa 2021).

morphology.endpoint: In 3D: thin-walled, clear cystic organoids and branching tubular structures in Matrigel. In 2D on feeders: a tight cobblestone epithelial sheet.

protocols.name: Cholangiocyte-like-cell organoids via SOX9+ progenitors (Vallier lab)
protocols.principle: Chemically defined endoderm is taken through foregut and hepatoblast stages, steered to biliary progenitors with FGF10, Activin and retinoic acid, then matured as organoids in Matrigel with EGF.

protocols.start_requirements: hPSC maintained in CDM-PVA with Activin (10 ng/mL) and FGF2 (12 ng/mL), passaged as 50-100-cell clumps with collagenase/dispase onto gelatin-coated plates; 500,000-1,000,000 cells per 10 cm dish for differentiation, grown until ready. protocols.name: Hepatoblast co-culture on OP9-Jagged1, then RA and Noggin/forskolin/ROCK inhibitor for ciliated cells (Keller/Ogawa)

cell_types.notes: Two families of method exist: fully defined organoids (Sampaziotis) and Notch-ligand co-culture giving ciliated monolayers or cysts (Ogawa). cell_types.name: Pancreatic beta cells / islets
cell_types.summary: Beta cells are the insulin-secreting endocrine cells of the pancreatic islets. hPSC-derived beta cells and islet-like clusters are used for diabetes modelling, drug and toxicity studies, and cell-replacement therapy.
cell_types.maturation_note: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion appears 10-14 days into the final stage and peaks around day 14 of that stage; function declines after extended culture.

morphology.endpoint: Planar: rounded, enlarged, slightly golden endocrine cells in a monolayer with some holes. After aggregation or in suspension: smooth, compact islet-like clusters of roughly 150-250 µm.

protocols.name: Six-stage planar protocol with latrunculin A (Millman lab)
protocols.principle: The whole differentiation is run as a monolayer; because stiff plastic keeps actin polymerised and blocks NEUROG3, a 24 h latrunculin A pulse at the start of endocrine induction releases endocrine commitment. Cells mature in an enriched serum-free medium and can be aggregated into clusters.

source.authors: Hogrebe NJ, Maxwell KG, Augsornworawat P, Millman JR
source.title: Generation of insulin-producing pancreatic β cells from multiple human stem cell lines

protocols.principle: Clusters grown in spinner flasks are stepped through endoderm, gut tube and two pancreatic progenitor stages, then given Notch and TGF-beta inhibition with thyroid hormone and betacellulin to make monohormonal, glucose-responsive beta cells at scale.

cell_types.name: Airway epithelium (basal, ciliated, secretory)

cell_types.maturation_note: Airway basal cells are sorted at about day 40-45; a differentiated mucociliary epithelium needs about 3 further weeks at air-liquid interface.

morphology.endpoint: 3D stage: epithelial spheres with lumens in Matrigel. Final air-liquid-interface stage: a tight cobblestone pseudostratified sheet on a Transwell membrane with beating cilia and patches of mucus.
